### Observed differences

- In the earlier window the five activities A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 each ran in about 16–25 in 100 traces (A19 44/200, A20 38/200, A25 33/200, A26 49/200, A27 40/200); in the later window each is observed in at most about 1 in 100 traces, and A19 and A25 in none of the 200. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009]
- In the earlier window, A43 (present in every trace) passed to one of these five in about 97 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions (A26 about 24%, A19 about 21%, A27 about 19%, A20 about 17%, A25 about 16%), the five rarely co-occurred with one another, and each of the five passed to A28 in 92–98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions. In the later window, A43 passes directly to A28 in about 87 in 100 of its outgoing transitions. [DIR011, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, REL019, REL033]
- The A43-to-A28 distance shortened by one step: the ordered pair A43 then A28 sat at lag 2 in about 97 in 100 traces before and at lag 1 in about 87 in 100 after; the pair A15 then A28 likewise moved from lag 5 (about 99 in 100) to lag 4 (about 76 in 100). [LAG007, LAG005]
- A10 ran in about 72 in 100 earlier traces near the end of the case (median position about 0.97), with A48 passing to it in about 69 in 100 of A48's outgoing transitions and A10 passing to A49 in about 91 in 100. In the later window A10 appears in about 15 in 100 traces at scattered positions (median about 0.43) with scattered successors, A48 passes directly to A49 in about 85 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, and the pair A48 then A49 moved from lag 2 (about 71 in 100) to lag 1 (about 87 in 100). [OCC004, POS001, DIR013, DIR003, LAG015, LAG014]
- A10's co-occurrence with A14, A15, A28, A43, A44, A48 and A49 fell from about 72 in 100 traces to about 14–15 in 100, and A10 before A49 fell from about 66 to about 13 in 100; these items largely restate A10's participation drop rather than independent differences. [REL001, REL002, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL013, REL014]
- A02, A04 and A06, each previously present in about 4–5 in 100 traces, appear in about 17–21 in 100 later traces, showing up as small new successors (roughly 2–4 in 100 outgoing transitions) of A14, A15, A43, A46 and A48, with scattered successors of their own. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]
- Minor shifts remain at otherwise stable activities: A14 passes to A15 in about 97 vs about 84 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A46 passes to A47 in about 99 vs about 85, and A14, A43 and A48 sit slightly later in the case. [DIR004, DIR012, POS002, POS008, POS009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, two segments that previously executed in most cases are skipped. First, the choice block between A43 and A28: A43 previously passed to one of the five alternatives A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27, which then led to A28, whereas now A43 leads directly to A28 in about 87 in 100 cases and the five are observed in at most about 1 in 100 traces. Second, A10 between A48 and A49 is mostly skipped: A48 now leads directly to A49, and A10 occurs only sporadically at varied positions instead of reliably after A48. The rewiring is shown directly by the successor profiles of A43 and A48, each backed by about 200 outgoing transitions in both windows, and by the one-step shortening of the A43-to-A28 and A48-to-A49 lags; the participation collapse of the five activities and of A10 and the co-occurrence drops agree with it. With 89 qualifying items against roughly 1 expected if nothing had changed, the evidence set as a whole is far beyond what random re-splits produce, and every item's difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits — although many items, notably the co-occurrence series, restate the same two differences rather than confirming them independently. [DIR011, DIR013, LAG007, LAG015, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, REL001, REL008]

The evidence cannot rule out that the later window reflects a different mix of case types (for example, a case variant that skips these segments becoming dominant) rather than a modification of how individual cases flow; also, zero participation only means an activity was not observed, so the skipped activities may still run in a small share of later cases. [OCC005, OCC007]

Other differences: The increased presence of A02, A04 and A06 — from about 4–5 to about 17–21 in 100 traces, inserted sporadically after A14, A15, A43, A46 and A48 with scattered successors of their own — is a separate difference not covered by the main hypothesis. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002] The small routing and position shifts at A14, A15, A46, A48 and A43 noted above likewise stand outside the main hypothesis. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR012, POS002, POS008, POS009]

Now let me understand the behavioural picture.

**DIR items:**
